## Natural history notes

A medium-sized marsupial characterized by its grayish fur, white face, pointed snout, hairless tail, and opposable hind toes. In Florida, it is found in a wide variety of habitats including forests, hammocks, wetlands, fields, yards, and urban or suburban areas. It is mostly active at night and feeds opportunistically on fruits, insects, small animals, carrion, and human-associated food sources, often using tree cavities, brush piles, or sheltered spaces for cover.
